study.question: Does separating the residual relevance hidden layer by task improve the combined memory/task model beyond both its shared-width64 incumbent and a nearly parameter/MAC-matched shared-width210 replacement?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: source inspection finds all four residual scorers factor through one width64 Linear+Dice trunk over 400 event/target/action coordinates. This is a structural sharing restriction, not a measured bottleneck or gradient-conflict diagnosis. R12 private-linear gives macro AUC 0.8310755947860231 versus g0 0.8303789178781177 and g3 0.8294837888998853. Relative to g0 its task AUC changes [click,cart,fav,buy] are [-0.0000803863,+0.0013664594,+0.0014729428,+0.0000276919]; it is not an across-task improvement. R12 mean-linear/private-copy/mean-copy score 0.8304714972/0.8306211409/0.8303725090: the single-seed 2x2 interaction is approximately +0.0003554657. R13 memory/static scorer contexts both lose to R12; their mean-routing cells also lose. R14 blocking click/aux/both hidden gradients scores 0.8308403373/0.8305847950/0.8305824964, all below open 0.8310755948. These results oppose the tested stop-gradient remedy, without establishing the absence of interference. R14 open exactly replays R12 at the same seed and is not an independent replication. Hypothesis: retaining all learning paths but giving each task its own first nonlinear relevance basis may preserve task information that width64 sharing cannot express efficiently. Shared-width210 tests generic extra capacity as the main alternative. No new performance is observed in this phase.

nearest_work.difference: Retain its complete joint/collapsed feedback memory, summaries, JointBlock and towers. The proposed change is confined to the already-added residual relevance scorer, not a new memory mechanism. Source hash matches the supplied receipt.

Its scorer construction and _task_pool were inspected: shared first hidden layer, independent second layers/outputs, private signed content plus projected linear-rank sum. Retain the latter paths and test separating only the first hidden layer.
Closest executable parent replay. Retain open gradients and every forward helper except the declared trunk-selection branch. No claim that observed gradients conflict.

Read archived primary text lines260-299, SHA256 83fb9eeca31e2fa3c557b6f08b893ad0018cefb33da6e00952136b9ce17e607e. Retain unnormalized target-conditioned pooling and Dice in a four-task field adaptation; task-private residual hidden layers are not claimed novel.

Read pinned benchmark primary implementation lines204-313 (commit90bb99a60724e975ec565836266fd86dcad0039d). It uses repeated category/sequence/task hub aggregation and affine broadcast; this study changes one local event scorer layer and adds no hubs or iterative exchanges. This is a benchmark-code comparison, not a verified comparison to original INFNet. paper:infnet resolves to provenance only; original-paper priority remains unverified.

Read pinned Dice: non-affine BatchNorm plus one learned alpha per coordinate. Use this for parameter estimates and account for independent private running statistics; do not replace activation or normalization.

All g3 content-plus-projected-linear task summaries and private score routing

study.proposed_difference: Replace only the residual first-layer sharing rule: candidate has four independent width64 Linear(400,64)+Dice trunks; each task consumes exactly one. Task0 retains task_trunk; other tasks own deep copies made after all inherited initialization and before model_to_device, with distinct parameter storage and Dice buffers. Copies start identically to the inherited trunk, consume no RNG and can diverge through their distinct scorer heads and losses. The capacity replacement has one shared width210 trunk and four width210->32 scorer heads. Both preserve two hidden layers, zero final scorer outputs, linear extra summary and all g0 paths. Each standalone file implements both sharing modes; CONFIG/defaults select the submitted arm. Narrow shared mode width64 is available for host replay against R14, but is not an additional proposed training job. No paper-priority claim is made. Availability audit: this proposal phase exposes public model/framework source, scoped validation receipts and the host candidate API; no raw parquet, executable trainer, PyTorch or test feedback is supplied. Baseline, both imported source bests and R14-open source hashes match receipts. Dataset identity/protocol are inherited host contracts, not parquet digests independently reverified here. No authorized memory-write command or validate_task.py interface is registered; proposal.json retains the prospective evidence and revision record.
predictions: Private64 will exceed 0.8310755947860231 macro validation AUC and shared210 if task specialization is useful beyond extra capacity. Macro Logloss and all four task AUC/Logloss deltas against DIN, g0, g3 and the incumbent will be reported; no per-task veto is introduced.
If added shared capacity explains improvement, shared210 will match or exceed private64. Improvement over the narrow parent alone is insufficient support for specialization.

Private64 will start at the parent prediction function with matching inherited tensors and CPU RNG; cloned trunks/BN buffers have equal values but no shared storage. Shared210 also starts at the parent prediction function because residual score outputs are zero, although its internal scorer initialization has different shapes.

After opening final scorer weights in a diagnostic clone, an isolated task residual-score loss reaches only its own private trunk directly, while the shared replacement receives each task gradient. Shared embeddings/value paths remain coupled; full-graph cross-task independence is not predicted.
Any supported ranking should persist over two additional paired host-authorized seeds when budget permits. Same-seed deterministic replay is not independent support.
falsifiers: Private64 fails to exceed the incumbent or is matched/exceeded by shared210; then this implementation provides no evidence for added task-specific utility. A private win only against narrow64 is a capacity-confounded result.
Seed rankings reverse or gains are smaller than paired seed variation/user-cluster uncertainty; retain preliminary or null conclusions rather than claim a mechanism.

Changed input visibility, failed masking/current-action invariance, mismatching inherited states, aliased clone storage or unintended RNG advancement invalidates the intended contrast until fixed through the authorized host, charging failures.
Observed training/inference time or memory makes the candidate dominated at measured cost; nominal MAC matching does not establish efficiency.
alternative_explanations: Generic added capacity, extra optimizer coordinates, altered gradient clipping and initialization/optimization noise rather than task specialization.
Independent Dice running statistics and alpha parameters are part of the private nonlinear representation; this contrast cannot separate normalization adaptation from linear-weight specialization.
Shared210 can exploit all210 features per task; private64 limits each task to64 despite256 total features. Equal parameter count does not equal effective function class, nor equal measured runtime.
Single-seed validation reuse, rare-task positives and user-correlated impressions can produce apparent gains. R14 replay supplies no independent seed evidence.
Task-specific hidden weights can still interact through shared embeddings, memory, extra projection and dense gradient clipping; this is not a removal of all task coupling.
